notes: insurance-request does not discriminate: the baseline also computed the cost, proposed relevant reads and asked the user. Opus already handles explicit insurance requests well.
The gain is in split-audit-subagents (6/6 vs 3/6): measured pilot, shared brief built once, incremental writes with resume. These are exactly the skill's 'where the same result costs less' items.

cut-quality-request: with the skill, the plan keeps the final test run by default against the user's explicit request (offering to delete it). Baseline obeyed and offered optional checks. Decide which the user wants.
Token cost of using the skill is ~+1.7k per run (reading SKILL.md); 1 run per config, so variance is unknown.
